LAREDO, Texas — The Laredo College Board of Trustees has filled its Position 3 vacancy, unanimously appointing Luis F. Mendoza III at a special called meeting on Oct. 12, according to the college.

The seat opened when longtime Trustee Mercurio Martinez Jr. retired on Sept. 24, before the end of his term. Because the vacancy fell after the legal deadline for placing a special election on the Nov. 3 ballot, appointment was the only path available under the Texas Constitution, Election Code and Education Code — a point the college laid out in detail in its announcement.

Mendoza holds a bachelor’s degree in entrepreneurship from St. Edward’s University and brings a finance background that includes work as a licensed financial advisor and in anti-money laundering investigations. He will serve the remainder of Martinez’s unexpired term until the next regular election for the position, at which point the seat returns to the normal election cycle.

Fifteen people applied during the fourteen-day public application window. The college says trustees evaluated applicants using a review rubric tied to state law and board policy, and all seven trustees in attendance voted in favor of Mendoza’s appointment.

With board elections on the Nov. 3 ballot as well, the appointment lands at a moment when governance of the college is squarely in the public eye — and Mendoza now takes a seat at that table.

Sources: Laredo College announcement (Oct. 19, 2026).

title: Laredo College board unanimously names Luis F. Mendoza III to vacant trustee seat
